partners.mechanism_chain: THPO (HGNC:11910) —INCREASES→ thrombopoiesis signaling (GO:0030103); CALR (HGNC:13036) —INCREASES→ thrombopoiesis signaling (GO:0030103); SH2B3 (HGNC:10711) —INCREASES→ thrombopoiesis signaling (GO:0030103); thrombopoiesis signaling (GO:0030103) —LEADS_TO→ thrombocythemia (HP:0001873); COL1A1 (HGNC:2203) —DISRUPTS→ collagen fibril formation (GO:0005581); COL1A2 (HGNC:2204) —DISRUPTS→ collagen fibril formation (GO:0005581); collagen fibril formation (GO:0005581) —LEADS_TO→ osteogenesis imperfecta type 2 (HP:0002651). Gain-of-function mutations in thrombopoietin (THPO), its receptor (MPL, not listed as causal but implied in pathway), or associated signaling molecules (CALR, SH2B3) lead to excessive thrombopoiesis and thrombocythemia. Conversely, loss-of-function mutations in COL1A1 or COL1A2 impair the formation of functional collagen fibrils, disrupting bone matrix integrity and leading to severe osteogenesis imperfecta type 2. The shared pathway is collagen fibril formation, which is essential for bone structure and may be indirectly affected by dysregulation of megakaryopoiesis and platelet function, although the primary causal genes are distinct and the functional directions are opposite.
